section_summary: This section completes annexes to a July 1937 Embassy despatch detailing Japan’s general and special account budgets and continuing expenditures for 1937–38. Subsequent records track supplementary military budgets during the conflict in China, controls on finance and trade, and American concern about bank credits secured by Japanese gold in transit.

subfiles.title: General account continuing expenditures, 1937–38
subfiles.about: The annex itemizes multiyear appropriations in Japan’s general account.
subfiles.summary: This continuation lists annual allotments for Army and Navy armament, warships, aviation, and reconstruction, followed by justice, education, agriculture, industry, and communications projects. It records previously authorized amounts, revisions, and scheduled disbursements extending into later fiscal years.

subfiles.title: Special Account Budget
subfiles.about: The enclosure presents 1937–38 revenues and expenditures for Japan’s special accounts.
subfiles.summary: Tables cover national debt amortization, public loans, the mint and monopolies, military arsenals, universities, agriculture, communications, railways, and overseas administrations. Separate accounts detail Kwantung, Korea, Taiwan, Karafuto, and the South Sea Islands, including loans, taxes, transfers, and construction spending.

subfiles.title: Special Account Budget: Continuing Expenditure for 1937–38
subfiles.about: The enclosure schedules multiyear spending under Japan’s special accounts.
subfiles.summary: It gives revised totals and annual allotments for postal, university, telephone, railway, harbor, and other construction. Colonial accounts cover extensive projects in Korea, Taiwan, Karafuto, and Palau, including roads, flood control, communications, hospitals, and public buildings.

subfiles.title: File note on North China tax and military budgets
subfiles.about: The note cross-references Grew’s telegram on new taxes and military appropriations.
subfiles.summary: Notes a proposed ¥102 million tax increase and a further ¥300 million military budget.

subfiles.title: Telegram 244 on North China operations and financing
subfiles.about: Grew reports naval information and new taxes intended to finance operations in North China.
subfiles.summary: The Navy Department disputes reports about Third Fleet threats and reinforcements. Grew reports a temporary tax increase expected to yield ¥102 million and a proposed ¥300 million supplementary military budget.

subfiles.title: Despatch 2531 on supplementary Japanese budgets
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Grew describes the second, third, and proposed fourth supplementary budgets.
subfiles.summary: The second replenishes depleted reserves; the third funds general accounts and disposes of gold revaluation profits. The proposed fourth funds the North China conflict, with large Army and Navy allotments.

subfiles.title: Lower House Votes Additional Budgets
subfiles.about: The article reports lower-house approval of the second and third supplementary budgets.
subfiles.summary: Reports appropriations, debate over taxes and soldiers’ families, and a warning about using reserve funds.

subfiles.title: North China Budget Set at ¥419,600,000 in Formal Decision
subfiles.about: The article reports the Cabinet’s fourth supplementary budget for the North China conflict.
subfiles.summary: Gives departmental allotments, projected bond financing, and the expected Diet approval procedure.

subfiles.title: File note on government finance
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a despatch on exchange permits and China operations budgets.
subfiles.summary: Notes a lower permit exemption limit and two budgets financing operations in China.

subfiles.title: Conversation on loans to the Yokohama Specie Bank
subfiles.about: Harrison reports differing American and London bank practices for credits secured by Japanese gold in transit.
subfiles.summary: London banks reportedly stopped advances against gold in transit while continuing loans secured by bonds.

subfiles.title: Department message on press reports of bank credits
subfiles.about: The Department addresses press claims that American banks were financing Japan’s war.
subfiles.summary: Characterizes the reported transactions as ordinary credits against Japanese gold in transit.

subfiles.title: File note on Japanese fiscal policy
subfiles.about: The note cross-references Grew’s telegram on wartime fiscal and economic policy.
subfiles.summary: Highlights extraordinary military estimates and policy changes prompted by expanding hostilities.

subfiles.title: Telegram 344 on Japanese wartime economic policy
subfiles.about: Grew relays the finance minister’s account of wartime spending and economic controls.
subfiles.summary: The minister calls for priority access to materials, labor, and capital for defense industries; restrictions on other investment, exports, and imports; tighter control of credit and privately held specie; and continued support for the yen exchange value.

subfiles.title: Transmission of telegram 344 to the Treasury
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards copies of Grew’s financial report.
subfiles.summary: Transmits telegram 344 of September 5 for Treasury information.

subfiles.title: Note on London bankers’ caution
subfiles.about: A State Department official recounts Wayne Taylor’s reaction to the London bank story.
subfiles.summary: Taylor attributed London banks’ changed practice to ordinary caution about possible risk.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Brock on Japanese gold advances
subfiles.about: Brock asks about risks in American advances secured by Japanese gold in transit.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck sees no special commercial hazard and suggests clarifying the London banks’ cited political reason. They discuss shipment routes and unsettling news from Tsingtao.

subfiles.title: Copy of conversation on Yokohama Specie Bank loans
subfiles.about: This copy repeats Harrison’s report about bank loans against Japanese gold and bonds.
subfiles.summary: Records London banks’ reported withdrawal from advances secured by gold in transit.

subfiles.title: Copy of conversation with Herman G. Brock
subfiles.about: This copy records Brock’s questions about advances against Japanese gold and London banks’ position.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck suggests seeking clarification of a reported political objection and discusses shipping risks. Both men regard the situation at Tsingtao as troubling.

subfiles.title: Ludlow request for information on loans to Japan
subfiles.about: Ludlow requests information on loans by American financial interests to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Seeks information about American loans to Japan over the preceding six months.

subfiles.title: Hull’s reply to Ludlow
subfiles.about: Hull directs Ludlow’s loan inquiry to the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: Explains that Treasury collects more extensive foreign-loan data than State.

subfiles.title: Referral of Ludlow’s inquiry to Treasury
subfiles.about: State forwards Ludlow’s request for information on American loans to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Ludlow’s September 18 letter for a Treasury reply.

subfiles.title: File note on Japan’s financial outlook
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a conversation with Japanese mission chairman Kadono.
subfiles.summary: Identifies a memorandum concerning Japan’s financial outlook and Kadono’s return to Europe.

subfiles.title: Note on Japanese bank assets in New York
subfiles.about: Lochhead corrects an earlier estimate of Japanese bank balances in New York.
subfiles.summary: Reports $14 million in net Japanese bank assets in New York and an unsuccessful experimental gold shipment to London.

subfiles.title: File note on a proposed Japanese financial mission
subfiles.about: The note cross-references a despatch on possible Japanese financial approaches to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Cites Dooman’s conversation with Yoshizawa and Grew’s promise to report any substantive approach.

subfiles.title: Copeland forwards letters on bank lending to Japan
subfiles.about: Copeland sends two constituent letters about American banks lending money to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the enclosed letters for State Department attention.

subfiles.title: Rasmus asks about threats and bank lending
subfiles.about: Rasmus asks about a reported Chinese threat and the identity of banks lending to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Requests clarification of both reports out of concern for American interests.

subfiles.title: Thornburgh protests reported bank lending
subfiles.about: Thornburgh asks for investigation of reports that two American banks are financing Japan.
subfiles.summary: Protests alleged bank financing of Japanese aggression in China.

subfiles.title: Hull replies to Copeland
subfiles.about: Hull acknowledges the forwarded letters and returns them with copies of State’s replies.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Copeland’s correspondence and encloses replies to Rasmus and Thornburgh.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Rasmus
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State responds to Rasmus’s questions about Chinese threats and American bank credits.
subfiles.summary: The Department knows of no Chinese threat to American civilians. It describes the reported bank transactions as credits secured by gold in transit rather than loans in the ordinary sense.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Thornburgh
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State answers Thornburgh’s protest about reported American bank financing of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Describes the transactions as ordinary short-term credits against gold in transit.
